v.title: Reedijk Calls Out the Easter Road Curse, Hibs Still in the Hot Seat
v.excerpt: Reedijk dismisses Easter Road’s alleged curse as Hibs chase a long‑awaited home win.
v.body:
## Quick take
Hibernian boss Marink Reedijk has blasted the rumours that Easter Road is cursed after a seven‑month home win drought in the Premiership. The manager’s flippant dismissal comes as the club’s fanbase grows increasingly restless.

## What happened
The BBC reported that Reedijk, who took charge of Hibs in June 2023, refused to buy into the idea that Easter Road carries a jinx. He pointed out that the club’s poor home record is no longer a mystical curse but a result of tactical misfires and squad depth issues. In a press conference, Reedijk urged supporters to focus on the team’s development rather than superstitions.

Reedijk’s statement also touched on the broader context of Scottish football, noting that other clubs have faced similar slumps without attributing them to luck. He emphasised that the club’s next priority is to secure a home win in the upcoming fixture against Rangers, a match that could shift morale and momentum.

## Why it matters
- **Mental Reset for a Young Squad** – Hibs’ squad is still packed with teenagers and fringe players. By dismissing the jinx narrative, Reedijk is trying to lift a psychological burden that could derail their confidence, a lesson for Barcelona’s own youth prospects who must overcome early setbacks.
- **Implications for the Premiership’s Competitive Balance** – A sudden home‑ground advantage can influence title races. If Hibs finally break the streak, the competitive landscape of the league could shift, affecting teams like Celtic and Rangers who rely on strong home form.
- **Precedent for Managerial Communication** – Reedijk’s approach contrasts with other managers who lean into folklore. His stance could set a new standard for how clubs handle narrative pressure, a tactic that could be emulated by clubs across Europe, including Barça’s own media strategy.

## What's next
Watch the next Hibs home match against Rangers. Reedijk has promised a tactical overhaul: a more aggressive pressing system and a reshuffled midfield. A win would not only snap the seven‑month drought but also signal a shift in the club’s culture. Keep an eye on how the new approach affects player performances, as a positive result could spark a resurgence that keeps Hibs in the conversation for European qualification.

*Source: [Hibs boss Reedijk rejects talk of Easter Road jinx](https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cr78274gepz0o?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss)*
